text:
Yes. Hansen Global Forest Change (GFC-2025-v1.13) records 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss in 2021 within this property (ASSET-A, 3,643.5 ha), or about 2.23% of the asset area. That figure uses a 30% tree-cover threshold and counts only events of at least 0.5 ha.

Context:
- JRC's 2020 forest map shows 98% of the loss area was forest in 2020.
- The MGAP 2021 forest map classifies 68.1 ha of the loss area as planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda). It classifies 13.2 ha as outside mapped forest and none as native forest. The loss is therefore mostly plantation, which is likely harvesting rather than conversion.
- A further 37.3 ha of loss came in patches under 0.5 ha. It is not included in the 81.3 ha.

Later years of the series (through 2025) were observed for this event.
